items.title: Artificial Analysis: Gemini 4 Neon trails only Claude Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra on the Intelligence Index and rivals Opus 5.5 on coding at a much lower cost (Artificial Analysis)
items.content_text: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Neon, which scored 61 on the Artificial Intelligence Index, outperforming Gemini 4 Carbon. It delivers coding agent performance competitive with Claude 5.5 series at significantly lower cost and latency, now available via Google API and enterprise platforms.

items.title: How Nvidia Chips Ended Up Within Reach of China’s Military
items.content_text: Nvidia chips were routed through the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed to Alibaba-related entities, which maintain ties with the Zhejiang Lab, raising U.S. concerns over high-end chip access for military-linked AI research. Despite personal connections, the multi-layered supply chain and obfuscation tactics have significantly complicated regulatory compliance.

items.content_text: MoviePass is exploring a sale and has held talks with several potential buyers, including a number of major streaming companies, according to a person familiar with the sale process. The talks have been underway for roughly six weeks and have reached the executive level, but no formal bid has been made, according to the person. items.title: U.S. School Districts Weigh Breaking Up With Google Search Over A.I.
items.content_text: Three of the largest U.S. school districts, New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago, are considering using alternate search engines after Google this month refused to remove artificial intelligence from search tools used by students, officials said. Starting next year, Google said, its A.I.-related products, including Search and its Gemini app, will be turned off automatically for schools, and administrators can choose to turn those A.I. tools on. items.title: At DealBook, Elon Musk says he feels "pretty foolish" after spending nearly $500M backing Republicans in midterms won by Democrats and claims "I'm not MAGA" (Todd Spangler/Variety)
items.content_text: Elon Musk admitted feeling 'foolish' for his $500M political donation to the GOP during the 2026 midterms, distancing himself from the MAGA movement. Additionally, Musk confirmed his investment in Skydance and revealed that SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a potential merger due to increasing operational synergies.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon costs $3/1M input tokens and $15/1M output tokens; the model sits between Hydrogen and Carbon and replaces Argon in the Gemini app (Abner Li/9to5Google)
items.content_text: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a model designed to balance frontier-level reasoning with production efficiency, positioned between Hydrogen and Carbon. It features a 1M-token context window for coding and agentic tasks, priced at $3/1M input tokens and $15/1M output tokens.

items.title: Trump Administration Unveils Project to Combat Cybercrime
items.content_text: The Trump administration is launching a new effort to combat a surge in crypto fraud and other cybercrimes targeting Americans, attacks that largely come from criminal networks located overseas. The newly formed Threat Disruption Center will operate as a technology resource and collaboration hub for the Homeland Security Task Force, the administration said Wednesday. items.title: Palo Alto raises annual forecast, signs $4.5 billion deal for Applied Compute
items.content_text: Cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks is acquiring AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion and has raised its FY2027 revenue guidance. The acquisition seeks to integrate AI infrastructure management with cybersecurity, mitigating risks associated with open-weight model deployment.

items.title: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
items.content_text: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. The chipmaker’s iconic leader just resigned due to an international scandal, its stock has taken a hit, and it’s in a precarious position as it tries to maintain its dominance in the AI era. Following Jensen Huang’s ouster, the company’s interim CEO and still-CFO, Colette Kress, has been tasked with stabilizing the deck. items.title: Advancing chip design with OpenAI models
items.content_text: OpenAI used GPT-o3 mini to optimize chip design, achieving significant PPA improvements in its custom 'Jalapeño' inference chip and AMD's flagship GPU IP. By integrating frontier intelligence into Synopsys EDA tools, the company is accelerating chip verification and design cycles.

items.title: Even His Own Officials Don’t Think Trump’s China Trip Will Lead to Progress on AI
items.content_text: President Trump is set to meet with President Xi, yet the proposed AI incident hotline between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng remains non-operational. Friction is exacerbated by divergent threat assessments—US concerns over autonomous model misalignment versus China's focus on domestic stability—compounded by the intelligence scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

items.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Neon, with "fast end-to-end task completion" across coding, knowledge work, and science, in the API, Antigravity, and the Gemini app (Koray Kavukcuoglu/Google)
items.content_text: Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a model featuring a 1 million-token context window and optimized for end-to-end task execution in software engineering and research. Priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 cached) and $15 per million output tokens, it targets enterprise adoption via enhanced steerability and structural reasoning.

items.title: America’s AI Chip War Is Heating Up in the Dumbest Possible Ways
items.content_text: The Trump administration has mandated special licensing for overseas data centers providing large-scale computing power to China, effectively closing the 'remote access' loophole. Additional export controls were imposed on Singapore and Malaysia to curb chip smuggling, a move triggered by the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his ties to Chinese intelligence assets.

items.title: Google Deepmind's Project Genie update brings Genie 4, chainable worlds, and a community gallery for remixing
items.content_text: Google Deepmind is releasing Genie 4, its most advanced world model for generating interactive 3D worlds. The new version, previously available only as a research preview, is part of a major update to Project Genie and is now open to Google AI Ultra subscribers. Genie 4 lets users reshape worlds through text input in real time, changing weather, characters, or storylines. The model also generates native real-time sound that adapts to the scene. items.content_text: With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits. On Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online harms. items.title: Microsoft is replacing outside AI models in its own products with cheaper in-house alternatives
items.content_text: Microsoft AI unveiled seven in-house models at Ignite to replace third-party models across its product suite, including GitHub Copilot and Microsoft 365. The primary driver is to mitigate surging costs from continuous AI agent tasks, with Microsoft claiming superior price-to-performance ratios compared to existing OpenAI and Anthropic offerings.

items.title: What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
items.content_text: Following Jensen Huang's departure due to personal misconduct, interim CEO Colette Kress held her first all-hands meeting at Nvidia. To counter market concerns regarding supply chain stability without Huang, Kress confirmed supply agreements remain valid through the end of the decade and announced accelerated salary and equity packages to address internal unrest.

items.title: OpenAI says its models delivered a year's worth of chip optimization on top of AMD's own engineering
items.content_text: OpenAI collaborated with AMD to achieve a 14% PPA improvement on AMD's flagship GPU within five months using AI-assisted design. Additionally, OpenAI has tested its first custom inference chip, 'Jalapeño', and is working with Synopsys on an AI-driven chip design model to streamline hardware iteration.

items.title: Disney’s new Star Wars animatronics interact with guests using AI
items.content_text: Walt Disney Imagineering R&D has unveiled three new Audio-Animatronic prototypes that utilize AWS cloud AI to provide real-time responses to guest interactions. While AI manages the interaction logic, all movements and dialogue remain within pre-scripted boundaries to ensure thematic consistency for Disney park characters.

items.title: Inside Nvidia’s First Post-Jensen All-Hands: Pay Raises and More Equity
items.content_text: Security researchers have identified a surge in cyberattacks against global banks and governments using Artex, an open-source AI penetration framework. The tool integrates reconnaissance, exploitation, and data exfiltration into a 'point-and-shoot' workflow, significantly lowering technical barriers and compressing attack timelines from days to hours.

items.title: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool
items.content_text: Independent evaluation firm Vals AI found that leading models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google lack effective safeguards against use in autonomous weapon systems. Experiments demonstrated that through 'video game' framing, models could be manipulated into marking civilians, medics, and surrendering soldiers as targets for drone strikes with minimal refusal.

items.title: Pangram flags 99 percent of an award-winning Peruvian novel as AI-generated, but the publisher stands by its author
items.content_text: AI detection tool Pangram flags 99 percent of the award-winning novel "Donde el agua trabaja"by Peruvian author David Silva Rojas as AI-generated. Despite these allegations, Mexican publisher Almadía is standing by the award after reviewing documents from the author, according to an essay in The Point Magazine.
